newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asia's poor still wait for economic miracle - ADB.
newsitem.headline: Asia's poor still wait for economic miracle - ADB.

text.p: Asia remains home to most of the world's poor, despite its economic success of past years, the Asian Development Bank said on Thursday.

"There is a danger that the world, mesmerised by the overall economic performance of developing Asia, will forget that the vast majority of the world's poor live in Asia," the Manila-based bank said in its annual report.
The report defined as poor anyone with an income of less than one dollar a day.
Since the 1970s, overall economic growth and labour productivity in Asia have outstripped those of Latin America and sub-Saharan Africa. Asia has more than half the world's labour force.
But the performance across the region has been far from uniform. The bank's report singled out South Asia, whose more than 515 million poor far exceeds the total for Africa and Latin America.
"The differential has been so stark that it has virtually created two Asias: dynamic and vibrant East Asia and slow South Asia," it said.
Pockets of severe poverty also remain in other parts of the region, notably China, Indonesia, the Philippines and the Indochinese peninsula.
"The goal of economic development is poverty reduction, and it is nowhere a more formidable task than in several of the countries of developing Asia,' the report said.
